correctness.rationale: With uniform vertex order the first accepted vertex is uniform; deleting its closed neighborhood leaves uniform relative order on the surviving induced graph. Thus the first-vertex probability generating function recurrence holds, with products for components by independence of their relative orders. On S(1,1,3), first accepting the center leaves an edge, while first accepting the nearer internal arm vertex leaves three isolates. A short leaf leaves an isolate and a three-vertex path; the farther internal arm vertex leaves a two-leaf star; the long-arm leaf leaves a three-leaf star. These residual laws yield (19,16,37)/72 at sizes (2,3,4). Exact independent Prüfer and order enumeration found (0,0,0,0,0,360) qualifying labeled exceptions through orders 1–6, testing all trees and orders rather than sampling. All exceptions had these arm lengths and counts (190,160,370) out of 720. The tree has exactly the short-arm swap symmetry, so this is one unlabelled type and 6!/2=360 labelled trees. The middle value is a strict valley and all three masses are positive.

evidence: The all-tree expectation theorem gives only a moment. Contat gives the exact law after averaging over the Cayley tree. Greedy Uniformity gives individual set probabilities in specified spiders with direct leaves and length-two arms. Uniformising studies positive unequal rates and full-set uniformity.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither first moments nor mixtures over tree shapes determine the conditional size distribution. The spider probability formulas do not include a length-three arm, and changing rates to uniformize the per-set law is a different question.

evidence: These are the inspected exact-law statements closest to the target distribution; the average is over trees, and the other laws are for specific families excluding the witness.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The generic first-arrival recursion is a way to compute the exact values but not a classification of when the support is an interval and the masses first develop a valley. The known exact laws do not settle all six-vertex trees.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the first fixed-tree interval-support valley in the random-order terminal size law, including the unique six-vertex shape. Related exact laws concern averages over trees, paths, or other restricted spider and decorated-path classes. None of the compared coverage gives the witness and minimal census. The identical catalogue entry is not a separate source of priority.
residual_risks: Pippenger's graph-RSA article was not available via the attempted lawful route. Older specialized graph-RSA tables or other unlocated exact enumerations could overlap; no historical-priority guarantee is made.

value.rationale: The terminal size law is natural for random greedy packing, and interval support removes the trivial way a star violates shape constraints. The first strict interior valley separates interval support from unimodality and from log-concavity even on trees. It gives an exact minimal, unique benchmark for shape questions about the distribution rather than its expectation. The result need not make claims for larger trees.
